name: Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation
summary: Rehabilitation is level- and completeness-specific, emphasizing prevention of secondary complications, strength, mobility, transfers, wheelchair skills, standing/gait when appropriate and lifelong health.

firstSteps: Review neurological level/completeness and medical precautions.
Check respiratory status, skin, ROM, spasticity, transfers and wheelchair needs.
Screen autonomic dysreflexia risk in lesions where relevant.
selfCare: Emergency plan for autonomic dysreflexia when relevant

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Plan is determined by neurological level, completeness, medical status and patient goals.
do: Review neurological level/completeness and medical precautions.
Check respiratory status, skin, ROM, spasticity, transfers and wheelchair needs.
Screen autonomic dysreflexia risk in lesions where relevant.

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Prevent secondary complications while maximizing independence.
do: Upper- or lower-limb strengthening according to level
dose: Strength: 2–4 sets × 6–15 reps for available musculature.
Pressure-relief practice: according to seating/rehabilitation protocol.
Transfer and wheelchair skills: repeated task practice with progressive independence.
Aerobic arm/leg exercise: individualized moderate-intensity bouts.
moveOn: Increase independence, endurance and community skills
Progress assistive technology according to function

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Protect insensate skin and osteoporotic bone during manual and exercise interventions.
when: Increase independence, endurance and community skills
Progress assistive technology according to function
do: Emergency plan for autonomic dysreflexia when relevant
dose: Progress independence and endurance before unnecessary complexity.
Increase community wheelchair or gait demands gradually.

manual: Joint and soft-tissue mobilization for secondary stiffness while protecting insensate tissue and bone
Avoid aggressive techniques in osteoporosis or areas lacking protective sensation
Gentle joint/soft-tissue mobilization can address secondary stiffness.
Avoid forceful mobilization in osteoporotic bone or areas lacking protective sensation.
modalities: FES/NMES may support muscle activation, conditioning or cycling in selected patients.
progression: Increase independence, endurance and community skills
Progress assistive technology according to function
Progress independence and endurance before unnecessary complexity.
Increase community wheelchair or gait demands gradually.
mistakes: Focusing on walking when wheelchair independence may be the more meaningful goal.
education: Teach autonomic dysreflexia warning signs where relevant.
Develop a lifelong exercise and equipment-maintenance plan.
escalation: Immediate medical care for autonomic dysreflexia, respiratory deterioration, DVT or infected pressure injury
